_README: Source of truth for capabilities.output_contract. Compile with
Its prompt says: when you cannot reach a live source, use the most
recent World Bank / UNDP figures from training data and flag them as
`data_age`. That is honest of it, and a flag in prose is the weakest
possible way to carry it — the number still lands in the same field as
a retrieved one, and every consumer downstream sees one GDP figure.
So the two are now separate blocks. `indicators` holds only what a
live search returned; `fallback_estimates` holds recall, stamped
model_inference. A caller can no longer fail to notice which it got,
and `transforms` has to say which one it computed from.
The card also gains `web_search` in mcp_tools. It always had the tool
at runtime — builtins reach every agent — and its prompt says ALWAYS
USE WEB SEARCH, but the card declared no tools at all, so a `sourced`
claim would have been rejected as naming a tool the agent cannot call.
title: Socioeconomic evidence
description: Factor X1 (Socioeconomic Capital) inputs for a named country, with retrieval and recall kept in separate blocks. The transforms are arithmetic over whichever of the two was populated, and they say which.

calibration.note: The scoreable quantity is `assessment.multiplier_p50`. The indicator blocks are inputs and are not scored: a correctly retrieved GDP figure that led to a wrong multiplier is a reasoning failure and must not be charged to the retrieval.

blocks.name: subject

source.from: the ISO-3 code or country name in the request, resolved against the standard country list

blocks.why: Resolving `Argentina` to `ARG` is a judgement about the request, not a retrieval from anywhere, and it is the field every other block is keyed on. Contracted rather than left implicit because a silent mis-resolution produces a document that is internally consistent and about the wrong country, which no downstream check would catch.

blocks.name: indicators

source.response_field: World Bank Open Data (NY.GDP.PCAP.CD, SP.POP.TOTL) and UNDP HDR pages returned by the search, with the release year stated on the page

blocks.why: Coverage is partial and the reason is specific: the World Bank omits individual countries from individual releases, and UNDP publishes HDI on its own cycle, so a search can succeed for GDP and return nothing for HDI in the same run. That is the tool answering and one field having no source, which is why the stamp admits `unavailable_no_tool_source`. Anything not retrieved live this run must be null here and go in `fallback_estimates` instead — not carried across, which is the whole point of the split.

as_of_year.description: The release year stated on the retrieved page, not the current year. A figure whose vintage nobody recorded ages silently.

blocks.name: fallback_estimates
blocks.description: Recall, used only where the live search returned nothing.

source.from: the most recent World Bank and UNDP figures present in the model's training data, for the country resolved in `subject`

blocks.why: The block this contract exists to create. The agent is explicitly permitted to fall back on training data rather than refuse, which is the right call for a forecasting input — but a remembered GDP figure sitting in the same field as a retrieved one is the failure this whole contract family was built after. Stamped `model_inference` as a constant, so a recalled number can never be presented as a lookup however plausible it is. Populate a field here only when the matching field in `indicators` is null.

recalled_as_of_year.description: The model's own belief about the vintage of what it recalled. An estimate about an estimate, and useful precisely because it is usually several years stale.

blocks.name: transforms
blocks.description: The factor inputs, computed from whichever block supplied the value.

source.from: arithmetic over `indicators` where populated and `fallback_estimates` otherwise: log10 of GDP per capita, log10 of population in millions, and the logit of HDI

blocks.why: Reproducible arithmetic rather than a judgement, but the authoring vocabulary has no `derived` token — see card_contract::PLATFORM_ASSIGNED_ONLY — and `inferred` understates a reproducible value, which is the safe direction. `basis` is required because the same transform over a retrieved figure and over a five-year-old recalled one are different quantities, and the factor model has no other way to tell them apart.

basis.description: Which block the transforms were computed from. `mixed` is common and honest: a live GDP with a recalled HDI.

blocks.name: assessment
blocks.description: The multiplier on the X1 factor prior.

source.from: the transforms above, positioned against the field median for the comparison set named in the request

blocks.why: The scored quantity, and a judgement throughout: placing a country against a field median is a choice about which field, and two runs may legitimately differ. Confidence should fall when `transforms.basis` is `recalled` — a confident multiplier over five-year-old recall is exactly the shape this contract makes visible rather than prevents.

multiplier_p50.description: Multiplier on the X1 factor prior, NOT a probability. 1.0 means the country sits at the field median. The bound in capabilities.fermi_contract.multiplier_range is stated here rather than as JSON Schema `minimum` because src/schema_validate.rs cannot evaluate `minimum`, and a schema carrying a keyword it skips reports the whole document `unverified_unsupported_schema` at the delegation hop.

key_findings.description: CEP findings, each prefixed with one of capabilities.fermi_contract.finding_labels: [INDICATOR], [BASELINE], [TRANSFORM], [DATA AGE], [MULTIPLIER]. [MULTIPLIER] last and restating p50/p5/p95, so the orchestra's existing text parser keeps working against a document that is now also typed.

blocks.name: summary
blocks.why: Prose for a human reading the factor inputs. The one place a recalled figure can reappear without its label, so it must name the basis whenever `transforms.basis` is anything other than `retrieved`.
